chunks: “The time of zuhr is at one cubit.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The correct understanding of these reports is what we have presented earlier in the book, namely that what they contain of the terms foot, cubit, and stature was mentioned only with respect to the place of the supererogatory prayer. We have already indicated that and cited many reports about it. That is not the time of validity, because when the sun declines, that is the time of validity; however, what is more excellent is that the nawafil be performed before the obligatory prayer until the shadow becomes one cubit. What further clarifies what we have presented is what he narrated:
From him, from Ḥusayn ibn Hāshim, from Ibn Miskān, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الظُّهْرِ: the zuhr prayer, the noon obligatory salat
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْإِجْزَاءِ: the time of legal sufficiency or validity in which the obligation is fulfilled
key_terms.الْفَيْءِ: the returning shadow used as a measure for prayer timing
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a cubit, used here as a measure of shadow length
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined past the meridian, referring to the sun’s movement at noon
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the designated time or appointed period for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: Do reports mentioning a cubit for the time of zuhr refer to the obligatory prayer time or the nawafil?
ai.summary: This passage explains that expressions such as a foot, a cubit, and a stature in reports about the time of zuhr refer to the performance of the supererogatory prayers, not to the beginning of the valid time of the obligatory prayer itself. It states that the valid time begins with the sun’s decline, while delaying the obligatory prayer until after the nawafil up to the point of a cubit of shadow is described as more excellent.
